scope: Same checkpoint, gradients and optimizer state; optimizer-only comparison.
gradient_distribution: torch.randn_like(parameter), seed incremented by one per update
measurement: Each variant restores the same model and optimizer checkpoint. The first update warms execution; the remaining two are timed.
artifact_scope: Numerical and timing record only; the local initialization checkpoint is not redistributed with this archive.

formal_observations.scope: Different real training windows before/after cutover, not a controlled end-to-end benchmark. Data time with prefetch is foreground waiting, not total background preprocessing cost.

kimi_recovery.resolution: Release unused CUDA cache after validation and, if necessary, before enforcing the unchanged 2 GiB free-device floor. Preserve peak counters and all computation/batch settings.

source.release_note: The execution release retains the previously bound strategy materials. Actual batch and program bindings come from each existing run; historical candidate values in the retained plan do not replace them.

preserved_contract: phase budgets, learning-rate schedule and data bindings

changes.change: Enable one-window CPU prefetch by default; preserve consumed sampler state and allow MINIFRONTIER_PREFETCH_WINDOWS=0 to disable. Native support requires one rank, a fixed input-token target, sample-bounded policy and a resumable mixture. MF support remains pilot/P0/P1/P3; P2 remains serial.

An existing token-based validation schedule does not repeat startup evaluation after an exact resume with completed updates. New starts, phase transitions and required phase-end evaluation retain their checks.

Router prepasses skip unused vocabulary losses while retaining backbone, MTP decoder and routing collection. Dense CUDA pretraining uses SDPA with the existing masks; QSA stages retain eager probabilities. The loop adapter copies active expert IDs once.

Dense attention removes only key columns masked for every query in a chunk. Custom image-visibility masks retain full support. mHC uses FP32 contraction instead of a five-dimensional broadcast temporary.
Stable route grouping replaces per-expert nonzero synchronization while preserving expert order, token order and empty-expert zero gradients. Vision grid and split metadata are prepared once on CPU.
Each independent package prepares vision integer metadata once and reuses sin/cos values within rotary operations.
Continuation uses the already verified model-local single-pass mHC FP32 contraction instead of the older broadcast implementation; checkpoint parameter names, order and equations are preserved.

formal_baseline.scope: The latest 100 recorded updates in each pre-cutover snapshot; medians are not a controlled cross-model benchmark. CE targets exclude padding and image features.

gpu_comparison.scope: Short operator forward/backward comparisons, without optimizer updates or added formal training tokens. Timings do not predict end-to-end training speedups.
gpu_comparison.measurement_note: All initial operator timings are medians: Qwen uses five measured repeats, DeepSeek three, and Kimi/MF two.

gpu_comparison.numerical_limit: For these nine initial cases, the largest recorded relative RMS/L2 difference is below 0.007; attention kernels and reductions are tolerance-equivalent, not bitwise identical. Kimi routing and all three vision comparisons are bitwise identical.
gpu_comparison.vision_limit: The three vision timings vary within roughly 6%; MF1.1 did not show a speedup in this short measurement.
gpu_comparison.seed_scope: Each benchmark group seeds once before its ordered cases: Qwen 2941, DeepSeek 493, and Kimi/MF 604; cases within a group do not reseed.

verification.parameter_bindings: Six resolved configurations and optimizer parameter/group orders match the original runs; four native program bindings match.

formal_after.scope: Preliminary medians from distinct real data windows, not a controlled end-to-end benchmark. Before uses 100 logged updates per model; after uses up to 50. Qwen has only three records after the GDN switch, so its result is especially preliminary.
formal_after.token_denominator: main cross-entropy targets, excluding padding and image features
formal_after.data_time_interpretation: Foreground waiting after prefetch; excludes background preparation overlapped with model execution.

qwen_gdn_followup.change: Use the verified FLA chunk GDN kernel for supported uncached CUDA BF16 execution. Preserve projections, convolution, Q/K normalization, gates, head mapping, padding mask and FP32 recurrent state. CPU, cached inference and unsupported inputs retain the torch reference.

gpu.precision: FP32 parameters/inputs with BF16 autocast; FP32 gate and recurrent state
gpu.scope: one uncached GDN layer with right padding; no optimizer or learning trial
gpu.interpretation: The approximately 6.3x ratio is for one GDN layer, not a full optimizer update or end-to-end training. FP32 state semantics are preserved; fused BF16 execution has measured rounding differences.

resume_control_followup.issue: A pause-marker cleanup ordering race caused each of the two newly resumed MF processes to finish one optimizer update and then pause again.
resume_control_followup.checkpoint_status: Both completed updates were saved in complete resumable checkpoints; no update was lost.
resume_control_followup.correction: Correct the pause-marker cleanup order before launching the next process.

fixed_validation.interpretation: The recorded loss is indexer KL, aggregated by the evaluator with CE weights. The fixed main-LM NLL is unchanged. Training consumes input tokens, not main CE; the 2.5B main-CE budget is unchanged.

d4_conversion.scope: Eight fixed held-out contexts, 11300 CE targets, with CE-weighted overall and domain NLL. The 5% overall and 10% per-domain limits are local continuation choices, not official thresholds or a capability pass. Each domain has only one or two contexts; no full-validation conclusion or confidence interval is established. Captured teacher attention mass and top-k recall were not measured; indexer KL does not replace them.

initial_microbatch8_failure.cause: CUDA OOM during backward before the first optimizer update

d4_execution.recovery: Initialize from the unchanged complete D3 checkpoint; only reduce microbatch and accumulate more microbatches. Preserve model, data, global input budget, learning-rate schedule, optimizer moments and RNG. Conversion report is reused; floating-point reductions are not claimed bitwise identical.
